arguments.command:
kubectl patch deployment orders-fastpath -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
kubectl patch deployment orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"track":"stable"}}}}}'
kubectl patch service orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"orders","track":"stable"}}}'
arguments.description:
Root cause: The 'orders-fastpath' canary Deployment (owner: payments-team, created about 3 minutes before the failures began) labels its pods 'app=orders, track=fastpath'. The 'orders' Service selects only 'app=orders', so it also picks up the canary pod, which runs http-echo with '-status-code=500'. The Service now has 3 endpoints: the 2 working orders pods and 1 canary pod that always returns 500. Requests are spread across all 3, so a share of checkouts (storefront /checkout → proxy_pass http://orders:8080) land on the canary and get HTTP 500. The canary's own annotation says it is 'Not wired into the storefront yet', but the shared label wired it in anyway.
Confidence: 0.96
Plan: First, take the failing canary out of checkout traffic right away by scaling 'orders-fastpath' to 0. Then make the routing durable: give the production orders pods a 'track=stable' label and narrow the 'orders' Service selector to app=orders,track=stable so future canaries can't join it. All commands passed server-side dry-run validation. I can't apply changes or send live traffic in this session, so I haven't applied the fix or confirmed checkouts work. Run the commands below in order, then check as described in validationIntent. (risk: medium)
- Immediate mitigation: scale the canary to 0 replicas so its 500-returning pod leaves the orders Service endpoints: kubectl patch deployment orders-fastpath -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
- Durable fix, step 1: add a 'track=stable' label to the production orders pod template (triggers a rolling update of orders): kubectl patch deployment orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"track":"stable"}}}}}'
- Durable fix, step 2: once the orders rollout is complete, narrow the orders Service selector to stable pods only: kubectl patch service orders -n shop --type=merge -p='{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"orders","track":"stable"}}}'
